public: # inputloop
The shop Corwin Brust and Bryant Frankford keep together, with Brigidt (GitHub: definitelynotaspren)
as a lab partner. This folder draws it the way topology wants to: one `TOPOLOGY.md` per thing, in four
kinds of container.
| pillar | what it holds here | folder |
| place | the hosts the work runs and lives on | `hosts/` |
| part | projects, components, files and tools | `projects/` |
| path | how work moves: mirroring, tangling, the atoms round trip | `paths/` |
| person | who answers for what | `people/` |
Three projects are private (`obsmage`, `obsmage-corwin`, `c4`). Each says `private: hide`
and keeps what it holds under a `## Private` heading, so the drawing names them and nothing more until
someone chooses to show them. The rule is in `spec/TOPOLOGY-md.md`.
Where a fact is not yet written down, the file says so instead of guessing.
# avalon

Corwin's workstation, and the machine most of the shop's work is started and signed on. The Windows side of the shop (Emacs for Windows builds, MSYS2 shells, the folder the agents land work in) lives here.
The app can draw it as a `server`. It is not reachable from outside; nothing here depends on that changing.
# code.bru.st
Corwin's self-hosted Forgejo, the primary place his projects are published. The canonical copy of a
project lives here; GitHub mirrors it.
# github.com/inputloop
The inputloop organisation on GitHub: the shop's shared home, and where people who work in GitHub terms
can reach what is published. A repository there may be public or private; each says which.
# gw10
The ghostwheel host behind ghostwheel.cloud and the literate façade.
The lab is close to taking on its management.
# gw15
A ghostwheel host named in the shop's host list. What it does is not yet described here; add it when someone writes it down.
# gw19
A ghostwheel host named in the shop's host list. What it does is not yet described here; add it when someone writes it down.
# gw26
The host topology is put on first: Debian 13, answering over HTTPS. The by-hand steps are in
`runcards/RUNCARD-2026-10-31-gw26.md`. Nothing has been run there from this repository yet.
# gw33
The ghostwheel host for the development site dev.ghostwheel.chat, where the `vibrobeast` account works.
# gw4
A small ghostwheel host that mainly runs one thing: Corwin's IRC bouncer (ZNC), with a healer project (`znc-healer`) that grew there.
# gw7
The ghostwheel host Corwin and Bryant share for the garden runtime.
# atoms-roundtrip
An OBS configuration is split into atoms, rolled up into `STAGES.md`, edited by a person or a tool, and
unrolled back. If both sides changed since the pin, the tool stops and names the atoms in conflict.
It never picks a side.
# egad-emit
How one set of tokens reaches every surface: `emit/emit.py` derives CSS custom properties, an Org HTML
export theme, two Emacs themes packaged for ELPA, and adapters for platforms that can be themed
(Nextcloud, Element, KDE). `make` writes them into `dist/`; `make check` measures every promised colour
pair first.
# mirror
How work moves out: everything is mirrored. The self-hosted forge at code.bru.st holds the canonical
copy (first push; merges go through Corwin), and GitHub, under the inputloop org, is where people can
reach it. A project that is private stays private in both places.
# profile-build
How the organisation's front page is made: the catalog lives with its builder and its check in a
members' repository; the public rows are cut from it into `profile/catalog.tsv`, the builder writes
the page between two marked lines, and the check refuses the page when it names anything private.
# pubs-refresh
How writing reaches the reading room: `sh refresh.sh`, run on the machine that holds the publication
shelf, copies the shelf into the `pubs` repository. The shelf is the working copy; the repository is
its copy, refreshed.
# recipe-tangle
`RECIPE.org` is tangled by `sh bin/tangle.sh` into `bin/`, `debian/` and `etc/`; `tests/recipe-check.sh`
says whether the tree still agrees with the recipe. Edit the recipe, then tangle; never edit a tangled file alone.
# transcript-sync
How the transcription tools travel: `PATHS` lists what belongs to the repository, and `sync.sh` moves
those paths both ways: `diff` says what differs in words, `into` unpacks them into a working tree, and
`from` rebuilds the repository from one. The recordings themselves never travel.
# bryant
Bryant Frankford. Made TopoForge and quantum3d5.
# corwin
Corwin Brust, `corwin@bru.st`. Commits are authored as him, unsigned; signing is his act, by hand.
The agent's part in a commit is a byline on its last line.
# definitelynotaspren
Credited by this GitHub handle. A lab partner in inputloop since 2026-10-25; NextTime-Dev is her work.
# NextTime-Dev
Community time banking for Nextcloud: post a request, volunteer, earn hours. An hour of help is worth
an hour whoever gives it. An admin, or a three-vote community process, approves hours, and every
movement of hours lands in a public ledger. It is definitelynotaspren's work (Brigidt), tested
on seven Nextcloud versions as of 2026-10-29. A browser demo is in `demo/index.html`.
# about-corwin
The source of aboutcorwin.com, a personal page. The repository is public (since 2026-11-01).
What it holds: `content/` (one text file per card), `src/`, `build.py` (Python standard library only),
`tests/` with `run.sh --prove-red`, and `DESIGN.md`, `ACCESSIBILITY.md` and `BUILDING.md`. It links only
public repositories. It builds in several places and is put on its host by hand.
A project of the shop. It is private: this page says only that it exists.
private: Kept on the self-hosted forge at code.bru.st, where the canonical copy lives. Holds the C4_ROOT idea
(registers read by path) and the tools around it; its tree is built out on gw33 under `/c4`.

public: # card-games.el
About thirty card games for GNU Emacs, from Klondike and FreeCell to Hearts, 500, Gin, Cribbage and
two-player Russian Bank against the computer. Every game plays from the keyboard, and with the mouse on a
graphical display. Cards are drawn as SVG on a graphical display and as Unicode glyphs in a terminal; a
menu switches the treatment and the computer's skill. 500 can be played live over the network. It ships
an Info manual.
Corwin's own, kept under his own GitHub account (mplscorwin) rather than the inputloop org. Installed
from MELPA: `M-x package-install RET card-games RET`. Code GPL-3.0-or-later; manual CC-BY-4.0, as its
README gives them (read 2026-11-01).
# corwin.cloud
Corwin's personal site, and the shop's showcase. Its front door is TopoForge itself, opened on a drawing
of the shop: one page per project the directory lists, made at build time from these files. It also has
a directory of the repositories, the packages, and demos of every inputloop app that can run in a
browser, staged from their public repositories. Served from gw33 since 2026-11-01. The repository is
public: https://github.com/inputloop/corwin.cloud.
# .github
The inputloop organisation's public profile page (`profile/README.md`) and the community files GitHub
uses for every inputloop repository that has none of its own: how we treat each other
(`CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`), how to get help (`SUPPORT.md`), how to report a security problem
(`SECURITY.md`) and what we hold ourselves to on accessibility (`ACCESSIBILITY.md`).
The profile page is built, not typed: `profile/catalog.tsv` holds one row per public repository, and
`profile/tiles/` a light and a dark picture for each (see the path `profile-build`). Corwin and Bryant
made it together; prose CC-BY-SA-4.0.
# egad
The house design system: one set of design tokens (`tokens/egad-tokens.json`: colours, type, spacing,
radii), rooted in GNU Emacs's Modus themes, which were built to clear WCAG AAA (7:1) for text. The gate
in the repository measures that claim rather than repeating it; corwin.cloud's demo of egad measures it
again, each time the site is built.
Emitters derive everything else from the tokens (see the path `egad-emit`). An archive node serves the
derivations the way ELPA serves packages: plain files, signed, found through `/.well-known/egad`.
egadjit is literate tooling: an Org file that tangles with or without Emacs, and a test that insists
the two agree. Corwin's; the colour values come from the Modus themes (Protesilaos Stavrou). Code
GPL-3.0-or-later; prose CC BY-SA 4.0.
# fourSwordsFromThePast
A Link to the Past as a native PC game with up to four players, same PC, LAN or internet, from your own
cartridge. You bring your own US ROM; none of the game is in the repository. Who made it, and its
credit line, are not yet written in its README; add them when they are.
# gitcha
A free, self-hosted forge for people and their agents: packages, git hosting, site hosting, CI and
functions, with two-factor sign-in on every account and a Claude extension that speaks it. It is the
front door of inputloop.com; the software is called Gitcha, which is why its commands and settings say
`gitcha`. Made by Bryant and Corwin. The repository is public (since 2026-11-01); its README says
which parts have been tested only against stand-ins.
# hello-taxgnomes
The Gnemonic Word Mines: a reading component built from a taxonomy at build time. Pick a word from the
word game's four tables and move a four-way slider: north simpler, south denser, east moodier, west
drier; the centre is the plain gloss. Every sentence says who wrote it: a dictionary, the game's pooled
sentences, a template, or a local model.
A worked example for egad: its egad hooks are suggestions, and the page works alone. `make` builds one
page, `build/hello-taxgnomes.html`, that runs in any browser; `make check` has two unfolders agree and a
second reader check the build. By Corwin Brust and Contributors. Code GPL-3.0-or-later; prose
CC BY-SA 4.0; the readings quote WordNet 3.1, GCIDE 0.53 and SCOWL under their own terms.
# journal
The open shelf: essays, one Markdown file each, named by date. It starts with two companion accounts of
the 2026 GNU Savannah forensic review, the discovery account and the second account written from the
record. Both are PGP-clearsigned: the signature is the integrity guarantee, the licence is the freedom
grant. `corwin.asc` is the signing key; good signatures bind to the fingerprint
Corwin's. The two Savannah essays are CC BY 4.0, as the shelf's README declares.

public: # obsmage
OBS Studio kept as a living, literate configuration, with plugins that sense the room. A downstream
build of OBS whose whole configuration is split into key/value atoms that a person or a tool can read,
diff, version and change, with credentials kept out of everything published.
## Parts
- `omg-atoms` splits an OBS configuration into atoms and joins it back (INI byte-exact, JSON parse-equal).
- `omg-compose` audits and rebinds multi-monitor captures by stable id.
- `omg-heal` plans, builds and heals Debian and source builds.
- `obsmage-core` is the plugin skeleton (designed, not built).
## Files that say what it is
| file | says |
| `README.md` | what works today, what is only designed, how to try it |
| `CONVENTIONS.md` | atoms and their classes, the `STAGES.md` seam, why nothing is reorganized automatically |
| `MODEL.md` | the direction, for a brand-new reader |
| `STAGES.md` | the one-file roll-up of every atom (two readers, two writers, a pin) |
| `AGENTS.md` | who commits, and what must be green before a push |
| `docs/REQUIREMENTS.md` | the requirements R1 to R8 and where each stands |
Personal recipes live in their own repositories that consume this one; `obsmage-corwin` is the first.
private: The repository is not public yet: https://github.com/inputloop/obsmage

public: # obsmage-core
The core plugin skeleton: where AR desktop control and camera calibration will attach
(`docs/AR-CONTROL.md`). Designed, not built.
# omg-atoms
`tools/omg_atoms.py`: `find`, `verify`, `split`, `join`, `rollup`, `unroll` over an OBS configuration.
Secret atoms go to a local vault (mode 600) and appear in anything published only as `@secret(len=N)`.
Tests: `tests/test_atoms.py`, `tests/e2e.sh` with `--prove-red`.
# omg-compose
`tools/omg_compose.py`: audits which captures bind to a display by index (fragile) or by stable id,
rebinds them, keeps screen-map scenes current. Never deletes; hides and reports. Every write is behind
`--write` and leaves a dated backup. See `docs/COMPOSER.md`. Tests: `tests/test_compose.py`.
# omg-heal
`packaging/healer/omg-heal`: the build healer. Follows `main` (the default), project meta, tags, or
signed tags only. Test: `tests/e2e-healer.sh`.
# obsmage-corwin
A personal recipe repository that consumes `obsmage`. It is private: this page says only that it exists.
private: One person's OBS rig, as recipe and atoms: `RECIPE.md`, `SCENES.md`, `STAGES.md`, `atoms/`, `journal/`,
and `hosts/avalon` and `hosts/giza` (the giza port is parked). Credentials are `secret` atoms and never
appear in the tree. Read `CONVENTIONS.md` of obsmage and `RECIPE.md` here before changing how things are kept.

public: # pubs
The reading room: a copy of the publication shelf, where finished writing lands. It holds `papers/`,
`posts/`, `persona/` sheets, the `canon/` and the `books/`. The repository is named `pubs` and the
shelf `pub`; both spellings are meant.
It carries no history of its own beyond refreshes (see the path `pubs-refresh`). A site's tree and the
shelf's working sets are left out on purpose. Corwin's. Code GPL-3.0-or-later OR LGPL-3.0-or-later;
writing CC-BY-SA-4.0, unless an item says otherwise.
# quantum3d5
A 3D particle, atom and molecule simulator for learning chemistry and physics in the browser, offline.
Bryant's. Needs a browser and nothing else: no account, no server, 0 network connections as of
2026-10-29. A Realism page says which parts are real physics, simplified, or faked.
# suit-crm-6-5-php-sec-backport
Patched PHP 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1 for SuiteCRM (the SugarCRM CE 6.5 lineage), against CVE-2026-109618 and
CVE-2026-109619. It builds PHP from the end-of-life mitigation commits the PHP project published on
2026-10-18 and 2026-10-21, pinned by full SHA (the build refuses to go on if a branch head moves),
proves that SuiteCRM 7.13 installs and logs in on each build, and publishes the binaries together with
the complete sources they were built from.
It is a build-and-prove apparatus: no exploit and no vulnerable code of its own; the patches are the PHP
project's, unchanged. `RUNBOOK.md` is what was run by hand on gw19 on 2026-10-21, in containers; CI runs
the same scripts. Corwin's. Scripts and documents GPL-3.0-or-later (one script Expat); PHP stays under
the PHP License 3.01 and SuiteCRM under AGPL-3.0.
# ta
Technology architecture: a portable, host-agnostic operating-model kit for AI help. The shippable is one
file, `AGENTS.md`, identified by the SHA-256 of its bytes (`AGENTS.md.sha256`): drop it at the top of a
new project, or attach it to a session, with a short instruction, and the AI grounds itself in that
host's public identity and prefers the host's own words and standards over its own.
`RECIPE.org` is the front door and the build. The rest is lineage, kept as it was: earlier models,
decision records, papers, a guide of techniques by kind of AI reader with what would show each one
wrong, and the run behind it. It uses public sources only. Corwin's; it works for its makers and has
not yet been reviewed by anyone else. Prose CC BY 4.0, scripts GPL-3.0-or-later, as its README gives them.
# three-phase-transcription
Recorded talk, in three layers that each cite the one below: quotes by time (`tr1qt`), subjects drawn
from the quotes (`tr2sm`), and a result (`tr3rm`) that names each seam and the pin that holds it, or
says it is still open. Every sentence in a result can be followed back to the second it was said.
`tr2vs` holds a subject layer against another reader's findings.
What can be checked is checked twice, by two readers written in different languages from the same
rules (`tests/tr-spec.sh` re-reads a set in sh and awk). The recordings stay where they were made; only
the tools travel (see the path `transcript-sync`). Corwin's. Code GPL-3.0-or-later (or
LGPL-3.0-or-later where a file says so); prose CC-BY-SA-4.0.

public: # topology
Draw what you have, from the files that describe it. Reads `TOPOLOGY.md` from the git repositories you
keep, sorts what they say by place, part, path and person, and draws it with TopoForge.
## Files that say what it is
| file | says |
| `README.org` | what it is, how to try it, where things are |
| `RECIPE.org` | the source of `bin/`, `debian/` and `etc/`; tangle it to rebuild them |
| `spec/TOPOLOGY-md.md` | the file format and the show-private rule |
| `taxonomy/pillars.json` | the four pillars, two axes, six tensions, as data |
| `AGENTS.md` | who commits and where work lands |
| `examples/inputloop/` | this drawing of the shop |
Private parts of any `TOPOLOGY.md` stay hidden until the component or the person says show.
The repository is public, on the `corwin` branch (public since 2026-11-01).
# topology-command
`perl/Topology/script/topology`: reads `repos.d`, fetches the repositories listed, builds the graph as
small files (`r/` and `c/`, written twice) and serves it read-only. Modules: `Config`, `Doc`, `Repo`,
`Graph`, `Taxonomy`, `Build`, `CSV`, `Server`. Every feature can be switched off in
`/etc/topology/topology.conf`; `ceiling = spa` leaves only the app's files.
# topology-www
`www/`: the front door (`index.html`), the app (`app.html`), the stylesheets (`css/topology.css`, with
egad's tokens in `css/egad.css`) and TopoForge. Works with no server (Zero Sharing). Checked for
accessibility by `tests/a11y-check.mjs`.
# topoforge
TopoForge, the single-file network and diagram designer Bryant Frankford made. It is kept in this
repository unchanged; improvements to it belong in Bryant's own copy first.
# topology-core
`www/js/topology-core.js`: the rules, not the pictures: reading `TOPOLOGY.md`, deciding what private parts
show, the settings kept in the browser, and the CSV TopoForge opens. The same rules are written a second
time in Perl (`Topology::Doc`), and both run against `spec/fixtures/`.
# vibrobeast
A memory Claude keeps on your own computer in plain files, with the skills, persona sheets and shared
rooms built around it. Ships as a plugin carrying three stdio MCP servers, and works as a plugin
marketplace for people who add the repository. Its skills are kept in their own repository,
`vibrobeast-skills`, so a person can take the skills without the servers.
A commit to vibrobeast is not complete unless its shelf on inputloop is correct.
# vibrobeast-skills
Written ways of working that Claude reads when a task calls for them; each skill is also a slash
command. 78 skills, counted 2026-10-30. Installs into Claude Desktop or Claude Code as a plugin. Each
skill says when it applies, what it does, how it can fail and how to switch it off; several carry
checks that are shown able to fail before anyone trusts them.
